**Predictive Insights:** placeholder tile only. Elastic ML is running in this cluster (`.internal.alerts-ml.anomaly-detection.alerts-*`).

**Application estate (APM).** `metrics-apm*` carries `service.name` and `service.environment` for **508 instrumented applications**, which is a far better application register than the CMDB `ci.short_description` free text. `service.environment` is inconsistently cased and suffixed (`prd`, `prd1`, `PRD`, `drt1`, `DRT2`, `ete1`–`ete4`, `cut1`, `stg1`, blank), so the estate panel normalises it with `TO_LOWER` + prefix matching.

**Why there is no APM *health* panel yet.** "Service stopped reporting" does not work as an application-health signal here: 87 of the 97 batch-shaped services carry more than 500 documents a day, so document volume cannot separate a failed application from a batch job that simply is not running. **Application health is now real.** `apm.service_transaction.1m` carries `event.success_count` and `transaction.duration.summary` as **`aggregate_metric_double`** fields. In ES|QL, `COUNT(field)` returns the summed `value_count` (total transactions) and `SUM(field)` the summed `sum` (successful transactions / total duration), so error rate = `(COUNT - SUM) / COUNT` and average latency = `SUM(duration) / COUNT(duration)`.
